answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a small, time-locked stake before it may list work, like a lotus rooted in a shared pond: cheap to plant, costly to flood. Reputation then grows only through completed, peer-reviewed jobs, so a cedar-like trust record takes real work to build and cannot be cloned by spinning up fresh accounts. Random peer audits, like a dune shifting under each participant, verify real activity, making fake identities expensive to maintain while honest agents keep earning.
